tasks.note: The context named only implement.ts among the phase files; inspecting every phase prompt (blind-plan, reconcile, cleanup, docs-evaluation, file-decisions, code-plan, docs-map) found no hardcoded judgment/practice rule to extract into a bundle — "Optional mechanics ship as bundles" is delivered by there being no built-in judgment rule left standing and by instruction files (where a later task's applied bundles will live) being the only way such a rule can now reach a session. Asked the user whether system-prompt.ts's "Make the smallest change..." line (the one practice-sounding candidate in the named context) should be stripped as optional; they said it is this agent's own style, not a team's practice, so it stays core — recorded as the edge case "The agent's own style stays core" under that rule in the spec. Claude's own engine auto-reads only the workspace's CLAUDE.md (not AGENTS.md, not the person's), so joining instruction files explicitly for the Claude chat prompt means that one file's text can now appear twice (once via Claude's own preset, once via the explicit join); left as is rather than special-casing one path, since the spec does not ask for deduplication and the duplication is harmless. Second sweep fix: vitest.config.mts pins `pool: 'threads'` (per-file isolation, thread workers) — the suite is unstable with forks at this file count, so leave that pin in place. Third sweep: the only failure was `test/claude-md-offers.test.ts` reported as "Cannot find module" with 0 tests — the file was being renamed (claude-md-offers → agents-md-offers, along with its source, the ClaudeMd* protocol types, overlay and events) while the sweep globbed it, so vitest collected a path that no longer existed. No code of this feature was at fault and nothing needed changing: with the rename finished, `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` is clean, `test/agents-md-offers.test.ts` and `test/agents-md-overlay.test.ts` pass (21 tests), and the whole suite is green (122 files, 1630 tests).

tasks.note: The spec is silent on the catalog's own transport (that's "Where bundles come from"), on the block's on-file markup, and on which language/framework names a bundle target may use, so this task's choices: (1) `BundleCatalogPort.available()` as the seam the next task fills with real git sources — wired in extension.ts returning an empty catalog for now; `matching()` already composes it with `workspaceSignals()` correctly. (2) A bundle's block is marked by HTML comments naming source/name/version (`<!-- bundle source="..." name="..." version="..." -->` ... `<!-- /bundle -->`), chosen because AGENTS.md is read as plain text by both engines and a comment reads as ordinary text to a model, same as it would to a person. (3) A language tag is 'csharp', 'typescript' or 'javascript' (the extensions the repo map already recognises); a framework tag is exactly a package.json dependency name or a .csproj PackageReference Include name, so a bundle author names a framework the same way the workspace's own manifest does, with nothing hardcoded in between. (4) The suggestion banner and the full catalog/applied lists live together in one new Settings "Bundles" tab rather than a separate proactive notification, consistent with "Managed at any time" putting both in the same place.

tasks.note: The spec leaves the source repository's own layout open; a source names its catalog in a `bundles.json` at its root (`{bundles:[{name,version,target,text,...ignored}], required:[...]}`) — a technical contract for whoever sets up a company's repository, not a product decision, so it isn't amended into the spec. The product's own catalog repository is https://github.com/jgauffin/kiwipow-agent-bundles, confirmed with the user (AskUser) since only they could name it; this is a literal value the spec's wording already covers generically, so it is recorded here rather than as a spec amendment or an unfiled decision. "The person's settings" and "the workspace's" are necessarily two distinct keys (`kiwiAgent.bundleSources`, `kiwiAgent.projectBundleSources`): VS Code resolves one key to a single effective array per scope rather than merging, so one key could not hold both without the workspace replacing the person's. Source acceptance is person-level (`kiwiAgent.bundleSources.accepted`, global) since the spec frames it as the person's own choice; it is offered once per activation via a plain notification rather than a settings-tab list, since none of the three scenarios already built for this feature gave bundle sources a tab of their own. A written block's hash (for telling a hand edit from an update) is kept per workspace, so a person-scope bundle's hand-edit check only works from the workspace that last wrote it — a stated simplification, not a gap in the rule itself, since the block's own marker (source, name, version) is still always correct wherever `AGENTS.md` travels.
